title: Colimit of residue triples is the strict henselization
statement: Let $R$ be a local commutative ring and $K$ a separable closure of $R/\mathfrak m_R$, regarded as an $R$-algebra through $R/\mathfrak m_R$. Let $p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $\chi:\kappa(p)\to K$ be a field map whose composite with evaluation $R\to\kappa(p)$ is the prescribed $R$-algebra map to $K$. Let $c$ be a universal colimit cocone of the etale residue triples [def-weil-pbc-etale-residue-triples] relative to $(p,K,\chi)$. Give its vertex $C=c.\mathrm{pt}$ an $R$-algebra structure such that every composite $R\to S\to C$ through a triple is its structural map. Then $C$ is a strict henselization of $R$ relative to $K$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization].

source.place: Tag 04GW, proof of Lemma 10.155.11: the filtered colimit of triples equals the strict henselization

proof.text: Construct tripleAsPointed by evaluation at the prime followed by the residue embedding. Conversely apply SpecToEquivOfField to B → K to define the prime and embedding of pointedAsTriple. The compatibility with R forces its prime over p. Both constructions retain the ring and the structural R-map. Construct morphisms in each direction from the same ring maps, since the two commutativity conditions are exactly the under-over equations.

Define a CommAlgCat R cocone d on pointed etale algebras using the legs of c at pointedAsTriple; h_rho proves these are algebra maps. For any competing cocone k, tripleAsPointed gives a ring cocone k-prime. Descend it by hc. This ring map respects R by evaluating hc.fac at the identity triple. The identity ring maps between the two round-trip constructions prove factorization using k.w and hc.fac, and uniqueness using c.w and hc.hom_ext. Thus d is universal with vertex c.pt; its identity algebra isomorphism witnesses the defining predicate.
